daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

A DPR member has rejected a proposal by the Deputy Chairman of the Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) to seize assets not listed in wealth declarations (LHKPN), arguing that confiscation could violate human rights. The pushback by Sahroni comes as the KPK seeks stronger enforcement measures against officials who fail to fully disclose their wealth. Meanwhile, analysts have called for wealth reporting to move beyond formality, urging stronger sanctions and confiscation threats to make the LHKPN system more effective.

  • Critics have warned that DPR oversight is hampered when party leaders serve simultaneously as ministers, raising concerns about the independence of parliamentary scrutiny in the current cabinet.
  • Hanura party has called on President Prabowo to form a technocratic cabinet rather than one based on political favours.
  • The Ministry of Home Affairs has stressed that the Administration Bill is key to producing accurate development data.
  • The National Police have responded to plans by BEM UI to demonstrate at Bundaran HI on 28 October.
  • Traffic management measures have been implemented around Monas and the DPR due to student protests today.
  • A controversy is ongoing over redefining corruption in the Anti-Corruption Law, with debate over the direction of changes.
  • The DPD council of experts has begun selecting recipients for the DPD RI Awards 2026.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and Singapore have agreed to form a joint task force to tackle forest fires following high-level discussions between the two governments. The agreement marks a significant step in bilateral cooperation on the transboundary haze crisis that has long affected the region. Indonesia also assured Singapore that controlling forest fires remains a top priority, and expressed support for Singapore's upcoming ASEAN chairmanship in 2027.

  • The National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) is reviewing Malaysia's offer to assist in fighting forest fires.
  • Indonesia has deported a Chinese fugitive wanted by Interpol.
  • The United Nations has highlighted Indonesia's role in shaping the global future and invited the country to help renew multilateralism to address world challenges.
  • Indonesia has set a target of US$33 billion in trade deals with the United States.
  • The Indonesian Navy and Customs have seized 1.1 kg of gold concealed inside a foreign national.

Other

State holding company Danantara has acquired hotel properties and land in Mecca, a move that Komnas Haji has called a historic breakthrough for the Muslim community. The acquisition is expected to improve facilities and services for Indonesian pilgrims performing hajj. This follows government efforts to streamline hajj operations after recent controversies, including testimony at the trial of former minister Yaqut, where a BPK auditor disclosed details about hajj quota determination and acceleration fees.

  • The Social Affairs Minister has revealed obstacles in digital social assistance registration, including residents lacking phones and fearing their benefits will disappear.
  • The government is preparing village cooperatives (Kopdes Merah Putih) to become distribution centres for subsidised goods, with state-owned enterprises making preparations.
  • A minister said the Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) program has created 1.3 million jobs.
  • Inpex has completed the Abadi Masela LNG FEED ahead of schedule.
  • The Environment and Forestry Minister has called for ecosystem recovery in North Sumatra.
